feedback.problem: The point $P$ has polar coordinates $(6,{45}^{∘}).$ Find the Cartesian coordinates of $P.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To convert from polar coordinates to Cartesian coordinates, we use

$$
x=r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

First, we calculate the $x$-coordinate od $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ x & =6\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\ x & =6\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ x & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we calculate the $y$-coordinate of $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ y & =6\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\ y & =6\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ y & =3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the Cartesian coordinates of $P$ are $(3\sqrt{2},3\sqrt{2}).$
